questions.prompt: What year did the Great Molasses Flood devastate the North End, and approximately how fast did the wave travel?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: January 15, 1919. Thirty-five miles per hour. Two million gallons. They say you can still smell it on hot days.
questions.npcReactionWrong: January 15, 1919. Thirty-five miles per hour. My grandfather survived something that sounds made up but killed 21 people.

questions.prompt: Paul Revere's house is the oldest remaining structure in downtown Boston. Around what year was it built?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: 1680. Place has been standing since before the Witch Trials. Revere was its third owner.
questions.npcReactionWrong: 1680. His house was old even when he bought it. Everything in this neighborhood has layers.

questions.prompt: The Feast of Saint Anthony has been celebrated in the North End since what year?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: 1919. Same year as the molasses flood. We've been feasting ever since. Sully's record was fourteen cannoli.
questions.npcReactionWrong: 1919. Same year the molasses came. We start every tragedy with a feast. That's Italian.

questions.prompt: What famous church has a steeple where lanterns were hung to signal Paul Revere?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Old North Church. And before you ask—yes, the steeple's been rebuilt twice. Hurricanes.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Old North Church. Christ Church is the official name. Everyone knows the poem, nobody knows the building.

questions.prompt: Before the North End became Boston's 'Little Italy,' what immigrant group primarily lived there?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: The Irish. Then the Jews. Then us Italians. This neighborhood's seen more flags than the UN.
questions.npcReactionWrong: The Irish were here before us. Then came the Jews. Then my family in the 1890s. Layers, always layers.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What is the main street that runs through the heart of the North End?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Hanover Street. Every restaurant tries to drag you in. Sully knew which ones to avoid.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Hanover Street. There's one street where every tourist ends up. That's the one.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What famous North End pastry shop has a long-running rivalry over who has the best cannoli?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Mike's. Modern across the street. Been fighting for decades. Sully said both were overrated. He was wrong.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Mike's Pastry. Their rival is Modern. There's a war in this neighborhood. Cannoli.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What company owned the tank that burst during the Great Molasses Flood?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: United States Industrial Alcohol. They were making industrial alcohol for munitions. The tank was poorly built. They knew it. Twenty-one people paid the price.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: USIA. Industrial alcohol for the war effort. The tank was leaking for months. They painted it brown to hide the stains.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What cemetery in the North End overlooks Boston Harbor and was a British lookout point?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Copp's Hill. British soldiers watched Charlestown burn from there. You can still see bullet holes in some headstones. Target practice.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Copp's Hill Burying Ground. The British used it as a lookout. Shot at the headstones for fun. History has layers of cruelty.

alternateQuestions.prompt: How many summer festivals and feasts does the North End celebrate each year?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: More than a dozen. Every weekend, different saint, different procession. This neighborhood celebrates everything.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: We never stop celebrating. Saint Anthony, Madonna del Soccorso, Fisherman's Feast... the list goes on. That's the Italian way.

redemptionChallenge.instructions: Match the pasta shape to its correct Italian name. Match 6 of 8 pairs.
redemptionChallenge.npcPassResponse: Okay, okay. You know your pasta. Maybe Sully taught you something after all.
redemptionChallenge.npcFailResponse: You called farfalle 'bowties.' My grandmother is spinning in her grave. Come back when you've learned something.
